adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 — When the credential comes from federated storage, nothing marks the used code as consumed: only the local provider's isValid removes a code, and this path only calls removeStoredCredentialById, so a federated recovery code can be replayed forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for recovery codes stored in federated/user storage: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` now prefers `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and is used by `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`. But the only federated/user-storage implementation shown (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`) validates recovery codes via `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)` and does not update the credential data to remove/consume the used code (nor otherwise mark it used). Nothing in the diff adds a consumption mechanism for federated recovery codes, so a federated recovery code can be reused indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, any existing local recovery-codes credential is left in place, and UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to local validators, so codes that should have been revoked by regeneration still authenticate.

adjudication.rationale: In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(), if user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential) returns true (i.e., user storage/federated storage accepted the update), the code does not remove/disable any pre-existing local (KC DB) recovery-codes credential for the same user/type; it just logs and returns. This can leave two recovery-codes credentials (federated + local) active. Since the diff does not show any cleanup elsewhere and RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() only affects lookup (prefers federated) rather than guaranteeing validation is restricted to the newest credential, older local codes may remain usable depending on how credentialManager().isValid/validation traverses credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:58 — getCredential always prefers a federated credential over a local one, so a user with both stores is shown the federated code number, the used-up local credential is never removed, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is never triggered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` intentionally checks federated credentials first and falls back to local (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst().or(() -> getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst())`). However, the claimed downstream effects (showing a federated code number being wrong, local “used-up” credential never removed, and `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` never being triggered) are not evidenced anywhere in this diff—there is no logic here about removing local credentials or triggering required actions based on credential presence. The preference order appears explicit/intentional per the new method’s Javadoc.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — The reference provider's isValid accepts any code in the list regardless of which code number was requested and never removes it, which models an insecure, replayable contract for provider authors.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` adds recovery-codes validation by deserializing a stored JSON `List` and returning `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. This (a) accepts any matching code string without tying it to the UI’s “requested code number”, and (b) does not consume/remove the code from the stored list in this method. However, this file is a *testsuite* user-storage provider (backwards-compatibility test fixture), not production code, and the diff does not show whether one-time consumption is handled elsewhere (e.g., by updating the credential after successful auth). So it’s a real, diff-grounded concern about the fidelity/security-contract modeled by the reference/test provider, but not a clearly verifiable production defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:119 — Raw plaintext recovery codes are passed as JSON in challengeResponse to whichever user storage provider accepts the type, and the reference provider stores them unhashed in credentialData, unlike the hashed local store.

In the diff’s reference user storage provider (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`), recovery codes are persisted via `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`, and later validated by deserializing that JSON and comparing plaintext values (`anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`). In the reference `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` implementation added/extended here, `isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` only deserializes the stored JSON list and checks `anyMatch` against the submitted code, but never removes/updates the stored list after a successful use. No core-side consumption/update logic is shown for federated credentials (the new `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(...)` just re-reads federated credentials first), so with this provider every recovery code remains reusable indefinitely.

While the finding’s specific claim about `removeStoredCredentialById` being invoked and JPA throwing cannot be verified from the shown hunks (that call site is not in the diff), the change does introduce a concrete risk: code paths that assume the credential returned has a local-storage id may now receive a federated credential lacking an id.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` explicitly prefers federated credentials (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst()`) and only falls back to local stored credentials. So if both a federated and a local recovery-codes credential exist, callers (e.g., `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` and `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`) will always operate on the federated one, regardless of which one might have been used/validated elsewhere. However, the claim about “the local validator accepted the code” and subsequent `allCodesUsed`/required-action behavior cannot be verified from this diff alone (those behaviors are not shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — The reference provider accepts any generated code (anyMatch) rather than the specific code number the login form asks for, and never removes it, so the prompt and the validation don't match and codes can be reused.

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), the newly added RecoveryAuthnCodes branch deserializes the stored JSON list and validates with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, which accepts any code in the list regardless of the specific code number the UI prompts for. Additionally, the method never updates `myUser.recoveryCodes` (or otherwise persists removal/marking) after a successful validation, so codes can be reused indefinitely. Both behaviors are directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:123 — Only the raw code list is sent to user storage; generatedAt and userLabel from the credential model are dropped, so the provider rebuilds the model with its own timestamp (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:199) and a null label.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the federated/user-storage path calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson))`, where `recoveryCodesJson` is only the serialized `generatedCodes` list. No `createdDate`/"generatedAt" or `userLabel` from `credentialModel` is forwarded in that path. In the test provider `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(...)`, recovery codes are stored with `createdDate = Time.currentTimeMillis()` and no label is set, and `getCredentials(...)` reconstructs the model using that stored createdDate and label (which will be null). This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency/data-loss concern for metadata, but it doesn’t clearly break authentication behavior since the codes themselves are preserved and the timestamp will typically be near generation time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:237 — getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-codes model with createFromValues on every call, so the stored id is lost (null id reaches account REST and the authenticator), and the model's hashed remaining codes are regenerated from the full list each time.

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage#getCredentials, the recovery-codes credential returned to Keycloak is rebuilt via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) from the stored JSON list, rather than returning the stored CredentialModel (myUser.recoveryCodes). The stored credential’s id is generated and saved in updateCredential (recoveryCodesModel.setId(...)), but that id is never propagated into the model returned by getCredentials (createFromValues has no id parameter and the code doesn’t call setId). This can cause the returned credential to have a missing/changed id compared to what was stored, which can break flows that rely on stable credential ids (e.g., account REST metadata / operations). The “recomputed each call” aspect is also grounded: getCredentials reparses JSON and reconstructs the model on every invocation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:231 — New getCredentials override and recovery-code support are added to a provider whose documented purpose (lines 59-62) is to stay source-compatible with the Keycloak 4.8.3 SPI, which weakens what the backwards-compat test is meant to guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new SPI surface usage to `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` (e.g., `@Override public Stream<CredentialModel> getCredentials(...)` plus recovery-codes handling in `supportsCredentialType`, `updateCredential`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid`). This materially changes a testsuite provider whose Javadoc states it is a Keycloak 4.8.3-era implementation used for backwards-compatibility testing (commented intent: future versions should work without needing to change this provider). That creates a real, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern about weakening the purpose of the backwards-compat test, rather than a runtime bug in the product code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:179 — Unrelated OTP behavior change (setId on OTP credential, plus OTP now exposed through getCredentials) is bundled into the recovery-codes change and alters existing OTP test behavior.

Additionally, the newly added `getCredentials(...)` method now returns the stored OTP credential (`credentialModels.add(myUser.getOtp());`), which changes how OTP credentials are exposed/listed from this provider compared to before (when `getCredentials` was not overridden here). While this may be necessary for recovery-codes support and not clearly a correctness defect by itself, it is a real, diff-grounded scope/compatibility concern because this provider is intended to emulate older behavior and OTP exposure/IDs could affect existing OTP-focused tests/flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:332 — Raw types `List generatedKeys` and `readValue(..., List.class)` (also at line 238) should use List<String>/TypeReference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:334 — Recovery-codes JSON deserialization is duplicated in getCredentials (line 238) and isValid instead of a shared helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:116 — Hardcoded provider id "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" duplicates RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID (follows the existing "keycloak-otp" precedent, but the literal can silently drift).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:121 — IOException is wrapped in a bare RuntimeException with no context, and `var` is used where the sibling createOTPCredential declares CredentialProvider explicitly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56 — Adds user/credential-manager lookup logic to a utility that previously held only code generation/hashing, and the generic name getCredential hides that it is recovery-codes specific and checks federated storage first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:123 — Copy-pasted flow helper has an always-0 `delay` param, a redundant `testingClient` param (it is already a field), an unnecessary delayed-authenticator step, and a typo alias "delayed-suthenticator-config".

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:410 — logoutOtherSessions` is only ever passed true, so the uncheck branch is dead code in the new helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19 — Unchecked Optional.get() throws NoSuchElementException (500 on login page) when a user storage reports recovery codes configured via isConfiguredFor/isValid but does not expose them through getCredentials (default returns empty) and no local credential exists.

Given this PR introduces storing recovery codes into user storage via `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` (using `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`), a user storage implementation that accepts/validates the credential but does not expose it via federated credentials would lead to `Optional.empty()` and a `NoSuchElementException` (500) on the login page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — When user storage accepts the new recovery codes, the previous local recovery-codes credential is never deleted, so stale local codes stay valid through UserCredentialManager.isValid's local-validator fallback and the two stores drift apart.

adjudication.rationale: The new `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` writes recovery codes to user storage via `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` and, on success, only logs (no cleanup). It never checks for or deletes any pre-existing local (KC DB) recovery-codes credentials when user storage accepts the update, so local and federated stores can diverge after a transition. adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 — For credentials served by user storage, a successful login never marks the code as used or persists that state, so allCodesUsed() is never true, the regenerate required action never fires, and the login bean always asks for code #1.

adjudication.rationale: The diff newly enables recovery authn codes to be stored/served via user storage (e.g., BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage supports RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, persists the JSON list in updateCredential, and exposes it via getCredentials). However, validation in user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` for recovery codes) only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)` and never updates/removes the used code or persists any "used" state. Likewise `getCredentials` always recreates a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` from the stored JSON list. Combined with the change to read federated credentials first (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now used by `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` and `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`), a user-storage-backed recovery code will remain reusable and the "next code"/"all used" state will never advance, matching the finding’s core claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — Exceptions thrown by the storage provider's updateCredential (e.g. read-only or unreachable backend) propagate uncaught and bypass the local-storage fallback, turning the required action into a 500 after other sessions may already have been logged out (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.java:113 runs first).

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` without any try/catch. If the underlying user storage provider throws (e.g., read-only, backend error), the method will exit via exception and never reach the local-storage fallback `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`. In `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction`, `AuthenticatorUtil.logoutOtherSessions(reqActionContext)` can run before this call, so an exception would result in a 500 after sessions may already have been logged out. This failure mode is introduced by the diff (previously it directly created the credential via the provider).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:121 — The IOException from JSON serialization is wrapped in a raw RuntimeException with no context, so the only failure mode is a 500 with no meaningful error.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the new code catches `IOException` from `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and rethrows it as `new RuntimeException(e)` without any message/context. This is verifiably present in the diff and would reduce diagnosability if serialization unexpectedly fails, but for a `List<String>` serialization it’s unlikely to be a functional defect unless an exceptional condition occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:244 — The deserialization IOException is swallowed without its cause or username and the credential is silently dropped, which then leads to the NoSuchElementException in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, if `JsonSerialization.readValue(myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData(), List.class)` throws `IOException`, the catch block only logs a generic message (`log.error("Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes")`) and then continues without adding the recovery-codes credential to the returned stream (it is effectively dropped). Downstream, `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` with no presence check, so an empty Optional (e.g., due to the credential being dropped on deserialization error) will produce a `NoSuchElementException`. The lack of username/exception cause in the log also makes this failure hard to diagnose.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 — When a recovery code is validated by user storage the core never marks the used code as consumed (the local provider's consume-on-validate path is skipped), so single-use enforcement relies entirely on the provider and codes can be replayed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff expands recovery-code lookup/usage to include federated (user storage) credentials via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` (used in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` and the login bean), and adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which first tries `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (user storage) before falling back to the local provider. In this diff there is no corresponding core-side “consume”/update step after successful validation for the federated-credential case; enforcement of single-use would therefore depend on the user storage provider implementation. However, the diff does not show the full validation/consumption flow inside `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (only the credential lookup changed), so the claim that the core *definitely* skips a consume-on-validate path cannot be fully verified from the shown hunks alone—what is verifiable is that the change introduces a new federated-storage path where single-use must be handled by the provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — The reference provider accepts any stored code (not the requested next one), never invalidates it after use, and compares plaintext with non-constant-time equals, so recovery codes can be reused forever.

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), the newly added RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel branch deserializes a List of stored codes and validates with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. This accepts any code in the list (no check against the “requested next” index/number) and never removes/marks a code as used, so codes can be reused indefinitely. It also compares the user-supplied value to stored plaintext via `String.equals`, which is not constant-time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:123 — Plaintext recovery codes are serialized to JSON and handed to the user storage provider via updateCredential, and the reference provider stores them unhashed (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:197), which sets a plaintext-secret storage contract for federated stores.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes `generatedCodes` (raw recovery codes) to JSON and passes them via `UserCredentialModel(..., recoveryCodesJson)` into `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (federated/user-storage path). The updated testsuite user storage provider (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` and `isValid`) stores and validates those codes by deserializing the JSON and doing plain equality matches, i.e., unhashed at rest. However, this does not strictly enforce a plaintext-at-rest contract for all federated stores (a provider could still hash before persisting); it’s more an architectural/security concern introduced by the chosen provisioning format and exemplified by the reference testsuite provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — Saving new codes to user storage does not remove an existing local recovery-codes credential, and UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to local validators, so old codes can stay valid after regeneration.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returns true (meaning the credential was written to user storage/federated storage), the code only logs and does not remove/disable any existing local (Keycloak DB) `recovery-codes` credential for that user. Since the diff also introduces `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` which explicitly falls back from federated to local stored credentials, this change can leave two recovery-codes credentials present (new in user storage + old in local), meaning regeneration may not fully invalidate the previous local credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:86 — The exhausted-codes check uses the federated-first credential from getCredential but removes it with removeStoredCredentialById (local store only), so it looks up and cleans up the wrong store and exhausted credentials may never be removed or re-provisioned.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator switching credential lookup to `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)`. It does not show any subsequent “exhausted-codes check” logic nor any call to `removeStoredCredentialById`, so the claimed federated-vs-stored cleanup mismatch cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — Test-double isValid accepts any stored code regardless of the requested code number and never consumes it, so the only test exercising the feature validates the double's lenient logic rather than real one-time-code semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch of BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...), the test-double deserializes the stored recovery codes as a plain List and returns true if *any* stored code equals input.getChallengeResponse() (`generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)`). It does not check the “requested code number” concept used by the UI/flow, nor does it consume/remove a used code from storage. This makes the added test (`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) able to pass even if one-time/consumption semantics are broken, so it’s a real test-quality/coverage concern grounded in the diff rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:259 — Test logs in only once with code 0; no second login asserting the next code is requested and that the used code is rejected, which would expose that federated recovery codes are never consumed (authenticator never updates the federated credential).

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` the flow performs a single login and submits only one recovery code (via `enterRecoveryCodes(..., expectedCode=0, recoveryKeys)`), then asserts the app page and logs out. There is no follow-up login to verify that the next requested code index increments and/or that the previously used code is rejected. Given this PR adds support for storing recovery codes in federated storage (`CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` writes codes into `updateCredential(...)`), not exercising “code consumption” across logins leaves an important behavior untested. However, the claim that this would expose a real defect (that federated recovery codes are never consumed) is not verifiable from the shown diff because the consumption/update logic is not present in the diff context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:241 — No negative test that an invalid/wrong recovery code is rejected for a user-storage-backed user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new positive-path test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest` that sets up recovery codes in user storage and then logs in using the requested valid code via `enterRecoveryCodes(...)`. There is no corresponding assertion/flow that submitting an invalid/wrong recovery code is rejected (e.g., expecting `AuthenticationFlowError.INVALID_CREDENTIALS` or staying on the recovery-code page) for a user-storage-backed user. This is a specific missing negative test for newly added recovery-code user-storage behavior, but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — New updateCredential-then-fallback-to-local-DB path in createRecoveryCodesCredential changes behavior for every user but no test covers the fallback branch (provider that does not support recovery codes, or local users).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new branching behavior in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`: it first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` and only falls back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` when that returns false. The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` exercises the user-storage path by enhancing `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` to support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` (so `updateCredential` returns true), but there is no test in the diff that covers the fallback branch (e.g., a user/storage that does not support recovery codes or a scenario where `updateCredential` returns false).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56 — New getCredential federated-then-local lookup has no unit test for precedence or the empty/local-only cases.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new logic in `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` that prefers federated credentials and falls back to local stored credentials (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst().or(() -> ...getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`). While the diff adds an integration test (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest#testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) that exercises the federated-only case (it asserts no DB credentials and that recovery codes exist in user storage), there is no test shown that covers (a) local-only credentials, (b) the empty/no-credential case, or (c) precedence when both federated and local exist. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern for newly added nontrivial lookup behavior, not a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:231 — Modifying the 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility provider with newer APIs (getCredentials override, KeycloakModelUtils ids) defeats its stated purpose and silently changes behavior under the existing OTP tests (OTP now surfaces as a federated credential).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the backwards-compatibility provider’s behavior and implementation in ways that can undermine its stated goal of representing an older (4.8.3) provider: it adds a new `getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` override that returns both recovery codes and the existing OTP credential (`credentialModels.add(myUser.getOtp())`), which will make OTP appear via the provider’s credential enumeration path where previously it was only handled via `updateCredential/isValid/isConfiguredFor`. It also introduces `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` for OTP (and recovery codes) credential IDs, which is a newer utility and changes how IDs are assigned compared to the prior code. However, the finding’s claim that this “silently changes behavior under the existing OTP tests” cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone (no failing assertion shown), so this is best treated as a valid test-architecture/fidelity concern rather than a proven functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:237 — getCredentials rebuilds the credential via createFromValues each call with no id and all codes unused, so allCodesUsed/removeStoredCredentialById paths in the authenticator can never be exercised by tests.

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, when `myUser.recoveryCodes` exists it deserializes `myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData()` and creates a *new* `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, then returns that new model. The code shown does not preserve the original stored credential’s id (`myUser.recoveryCodes.setId(...)` is set in `updateCredential`, but that id is not propagated in `getCredentials`). Also, the provider’s `isValid(...)` for recovery codes only checks membership in the stored list and never updates/removes codes, so “used code / all codes used” behaviors wouldn’t be observable in tests backed by this provider. This is a test-provider fidelity / coverage limitation rather than a product bug proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:420 — setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction takes a userId but hardcodes login as "otp1" (also hardcoded in hasRecoveryCodes check at line 460), coupling helpers to a copy-pasted OTP username.

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest, the helper `setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction(String userId, ...)` accepts `userId` but then performs login with hardcoded credentials `testAppHelper.startLogin("otp1", "pass")`, ignoring the parameter. Similarly, `assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage` calls `storageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes("otp1")`. While the current test creates the user with username `"otp1"`, this tightly couples the helpers to that specific username and makes them misleading/non-reusable, which is a concrete test design issue shown in the diff rather than a functional product bug.
